title: Grow Zedu's pipeline and turn its traffic into signups
description:
Zedu's marketing site has been worked on for being found. It has not been worked on for being chosen. Six goals in this project cover search visibility, page speed, metadata and content, and none of them owns the two things that decide whether a visitor becomes a customer: who the platform should be reaching, and what stops them signing up.

This goal covers both.

On the pipeline side: the audience is training and education operators — bootcamp operators, corporate training teams running cohort programmes, university and K-12 course leads — and nobody has identified them yet. The task types for lead hunting and press outreach exist and are worth fifty points each, and not one task of that kind has been created in this project.

On the conversion side, the measurement is in the site's own pages. The line "Launching a bootcamp? Let's build a pricing model that fits your cohort size" appears on both the homepage and the pricing page. The same "Got a Question? We Have an Answer" block is repeated on the homepage, the pricing page and all three product pages. The homepage embeds the full pricing table that /pricing exists to hold, and the same segment cards appear on the homepage and on each of the three solution pages. So the questions a visitor asks before they sign up are answered in several places at once and in different words, and the strongest versions of them are diluted.

Success means a qualified list of prospects with a named reason each one fits, at least one pitch sent to a real outlet that genuinely covers the audience, and a set of conversion recommendations for the duplicated blocks above, with the duplicates consolidated and the surviving version saying the thing more directly.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Map the signup funnel end to end and list the three biggest drop-off points with fixes
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Walk the path a visitor takes from the home page to an active workspace, recording every step, form field and page with screenshots, and read the analytics already on the site (Google Analytics is installed) for where people leave. It also notes that the home page's <title> is just "Home" with no share image, which hurts the first step for anyone arriving from a shared link.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Consolidate the pricing and FAQ blocks that six pages repeat, and write the survivors properly
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The second half of this goal, and it starts with what is already measurable on the live site.

The line 'Launching a bootcamp? Let's build a pricing model that fits your cohort size' appears on the homepage and on /pricing. The same 'Got a Question? We Have an Answer' block appears on the homepage, on /pricing and on all three /products pages. The homepage embeds the full pricing table that /pricing exists to hold, and it mirrors the three segment cards that /solutions/bootcamps, /solutions/schools and /solutions/universities already own.

So the questions a visitor asks just before signing up are answered in several places at once and in different words, and the strongest version of each answer is diluted across six pages. That is a conversion problem before it is an SEO one, and it is worth fixing with intent rather than with a template.

The deliverable is a duplication table naming which page keeps each block and which loses it, a rewritten version of every surviving block written for a visitor who is close to deciding, and the internal links that connect them. Where a line is genuinely worth keeping on two pages because the context differs, that is stated and both versions are written for their own context rather than copied between them. Every duplication quoted is copied from the live markup so it can be checked directly.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A qualified outbound list of cohort operators, each with a reason and an angle
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The first half of this goal, and the half nobody has started. A list worth working, not a list that exists: every organisation is qualified against what the product genuinely does well, so it can be worked without further research.

The qualification criteria are that they run a cohort or a cohort-based programme, the cohort has a fixed start date, they run live sessions, they have mentors giving feedback, and they need a shared workspace rather than a folder of links. Each entry carries the organisation, what it actually runs, the public contact route, one specific sentence on why it fits, and a suggested angle for the first message. The angle matters more than the contact, because a message that opens with the product is a message that gets ignored.

Only publicly listed contact details are used, and every one is marked for verification before use rather than presented as a deliverable inbox. The work splits by segment so each task is finishable, and each ends with a prioritised shortlist rather than a raw count: twelve entries with a reason attached is worth more than forty without, because the first number can be worked on Monday and the second cannot.

Where an organisation is a genuine partner rather than a prospect, that is said and the reason is given, because a partner conversation is a different message and a different ask.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A press angle worth pitching: what the completion-rate numbers actually show
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The earned-media route, which is the only channel that reaches a market where nobody is searching for Zedu by name yet.

The hook comes from sourced numbers rather than from a product claim. Cohort-based programmes with live sessions commonly report completion in the 50 to 85 percent range, against roughly 5 to 15 percent for self-paced equivalents, with the closest thing to peer-reviewed evidence sitting on the self-paced side at around 5 percent for MOOCs. The widely repeated 90-plus percent figure comes from vendors selling cohort programmes rather than from research, and saying so plainly is the angle. It is checkable, it is the kind of thing a trade editor can verify, and it is more useful to the reader than another launch post.

The deliverable is the pitch, the outlets it fits and why each one fits, a version adapted to each outlet's angle, and a sources appendix listing every figure with where it came from so an editor can check it in one click. A pitch with no specific finding behind it is a press release, and trade press declines those, so the finding is the pitch.

downvotes.reason: Same issue as the completion-rate press angle on the 5-outlet goal: the 50-85% and 5-15% figures are called 'sourced', but the delivery that used them (reviewed 22 Oct 2026) contained no links at all. Until each number links to an actual study, this hook can't be fact-checked by an editor.
Same unsupported numbers: '5-15% self-paced' is unsourced, and the '~5% for MOOCs' figure is misattributed (the Open Praxis 2024 study's own MOOCs show 12-44%).

The 50-85% vs 5-15% anchors were shown unreliable in a reviewed delivery: the ~5% MOOC figure is misattributed to a study whose own MOOCs report 12-44%, and 5-15% is unsourced. A pitch built on them inherits that problem. What works better: keep the pitch structure but rebuild it on figures that check out in the sources appendix, or on Zedu's own verifiable facts.

pendingIdeas.title: Consolidate duplicated FAQ and pricing copy across the homepage and solution routes to sharpen conversion signals
pendingIdeas.description: Analysis shows the exact same FAQ block and pricing tier pitch are duplicated across the homepage, pricing page, and solution subpages, diluting buyer focus. Approach: (1) Audit all duplicate messaging blocks on the homepage and solution subpages; (2) Rewrite the homepage section to focus exclusively on immediate value proposition and primary signup CTA; (3) Restrict detailed pricing tables and edge-case objection FAQs strictly to /pricing and specialized solution pages; (4) Provide a clear before-and-after copy comparison with verified readability scores. Done when duplicate copy blocks are removed and unique, high-intent conversion pathways are established for each buyer segment.
